transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
President Trump will campaign in South Carolina later today for GOP Senator Darlene Graham.
She was named to take over the seat for her brother, Lindsey, who died suddenly earlier
this year.
NPR's Tamara Keith says President Trump campaigned in North Carolina last evening.
Last night, he made a promise to North Carolinians affected by contaminated water at the Camp
Lejeune Marine Corps base.
He said if Republicans win the House and the Senate, he would order the Department of Justice
to settle all remaining legitimate claims.
So if we don't win, there's no money.
If we do win, you're getting it, and it's going to be finally over with that nightmare
that's been going on for so many years.
I don't know that I have ever heard a president so explicitly deliver an ultimatum to voters
like this, tying government settlement funds to an election outcome.
NPR's Tamara Keith reporting.
Russian President Vladimir Putin says he has freed American Stephen Hubbard from a Russian
prison following a request from President Trump.
Hubbard had been sentenced to nearly seven years in prison.
The announcement came as talks got underway between Putin and White House envoy Steve
Whitcoff.
They're focused on U.S. efforts to end the war in Ukraine.
From Moscow, NPR's Charles Mains reports.
74-year-old Stephen Hubbard of Michigan was detained by Russian forces in Ukraine in 2022,
and later sentenced for serving as a mercenary in the Ukrainian army.
He's now a free man.
Speaking before cameras, as talks with White House envoy Steve Whitcoff got underway in
Russia's former imperial capital of St. Petersburg, President Putin announced Hubbard had been
released and was already at the airport.
Later this week, President Trump said he'd asked Putin to release Hubbard, whom the U.S.
had formally designated "wrongfully detained."
Hubbard's release comes as Trump has lifted some sanctions on Moscow and openly criticized
Ukraine amid U.S. efforts to negotiate an end to the war.
Charles Mains, NPR News, Moscow.
Streaming giant Netflix is reporting slower quarterly revenue growth over the past three
years, and Pierre's Mandalit Del Barco reports.
Netflix co-CEO Greg Peters talked to investors after the third quarter earnings report.
"Our engagement is solid, but we know that we can do better.
It's our goal to go from very good to great."
Peters said they had to make some tough financial decisions, so last week Netflix laid off 1,000
workers, 6 percent of the company.
After handing them their pink slips, the company's content chief was fired.
Also ousted were the chairman of Netflix Film and six other top executives.
The news comes at a turbulent time in Hollywood.
Disney just had its third wave of layoffs in six months, and workers at the new Skydance
company that merged Paramount and Warner Bros. are bracing for massive layoffs, too.
Mandalit Del Barco, NPR News, Los Angeles.
This is NPR.
In Michigan, Democratic Senate nominee Abdul Al Sayyad has a new ad defending his Muslim
faith.
Al Sayyad comes after months of attacks, making fun of his name and trying to tie him to terrorism.
From Michigan Public Radio, Colin Jackson reports.
"Islam and terrorism are not related, but for weeks Al Sayyad's Republican opponents
have tried to link him to groups like the Muslim Brotherhood.
It's a claim he's vehemently denied and called unserious.
Recently, President Donald Trump said this about Al Sayyad, a Michigan-born and raised
son of Egyptian immigrants.
"His name is actually Abdulla.
Now Al Sayyad is hitting back.
His new ad accuses politicians of getting cynical without faith in our future.
"My name is Abdul.
I mean servant.
I pray every day."
Over 10 percent of registered voters in Michigan have already cast a ballot.
For NPR News, I'm Colin Jackson in Michigan.
The National Association of Realtors says pending home sales in September were down
more than 11 percent compared to a year ago.
Demand for homes is slumping as mortgage loan rates are climbing.
The Commerce Department says single-family housing starts fell 4.6 percent on an annual
rate in September, further reflecting economic gloom.
Pope Leo appeared in public at the Vatican today for his regular general audience.
It's been a little more than a week since he had part of a lung removed to treat cancer.
The pontiff rode in the popemobile to greet people, and he thanked them for their support.
I'm Corva Coleman, NPR News.
